title: Iberia to Chase the Solar Eclipse at 35,000 Feet in a Historic First
excerpt: The Spanish airline will fly an Airbus A321XLR above the clouds on August 12 to observe Spain's first total solar eclipse in over a century, livestreaming the event globally via Starlink.
body:
• Spanish airline Iberia will operate a special flight on August 12 to observe the total solar eclipse from above the clouds, using one of its new Airbus A321XLR aircraft.
  • The flight, designated IB1473 in honour of astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus's birth year, will depart Madrid at 6:45 PM and fly over the province of Palencia during totality.
  • The event will be livestreamed globally via Iberia's social media channels using onboard Starlink satellite internet, while researchers from Project Shelios will conduct scientific observations.

When the moon's shadow races across northern Spain on August 12, most observers will be craning their necks skyward from the ground. Iberia, Spain's flag carrier, plans to be above the clouds.

The airline has announced a special flight designed to observe Spain's first total solar eclipse in over a century from 35,000 feet, deploying one of its new Airbus A321XLR aircraft on a route specifically calculated to maximise viewing conditions over the province of Palencia in central northern Spain.

A Flight with a Cosmic Purpose

The aircraft will depart Madrid's Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas airport at 6:45 PM local time, timed to position passengers above the cloud layer during the brief window of totality. The flight has been designated IB1473 — a nod to 1473, the birth year of astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus.

At the controls will be Captain Javier Lopera Alcalá and co-pilot Javier Meana Fernández, who holds a degree in astrophysics — a fitting qualification for a mission designed to chase a celestial event.

Anyone unable to secure a seat will still be able to watch. Iberia plans to livestream the eclipse in real time across its social media channels, made possible by the progressive integration of Starlink satellite internet into its fleet, which provides high-speed connectivity throughout the flight.

Science at Altitude

The flight won't be purely for spectacle. Researchers from Project Shelios, a Spanish scientific initiative, will conduct four simultaneous experiments aboard the aircraft. These include studying the morphology of the solar corona, searching for Perseid meteors visible during totality, and broadcasting the phenomenon live from 11,000 metres altitude.

The most innovative experiment will be Project CORONA, led by Carlos Javier Rodríguez, a secondary school director from Extremadura. His study will analyse the human psychological response to a total solar eclipse — examining how the experience affects perception of time, emotional responses, and memory formation. It is one of the first studies of its kind to focus on the subjective human dimension of an eclipse.

"The Sun is going to be very low on the horizon and there is a risk of cloud cover, so the idea arose of proposing to Iberia a flight that would allow us to position ourselves above the clouds."

— Carlos Javier Rodríguez, Project CORONA lead researcher

Spain's Eclipse Century

The August 12 event is the first total solar eclipse visible from mainland Spain since 1905 — and the first from the broader Iberian Peninsula since 1912. The path of totality will sweep from Galicia on the northwest coast across a 290-kilometre-wide band to the Mediterranean coast, reaching cities including Valencia, where totality will last approximately 60 to 70 seconds beginning at 8:32 PM.

Spain is about to enter an unprecedented period for solar eclipses. After this year's event, another total solar eclipse will cross the country's southern regions on August 2, 2027, followed by an annular eclipse on January 26, 2028. After this trio, the next total solar eclipse visible from Spain won't occur until 2053.

The concentration of three eclipses in three years has sparked a wave of astrotourism planning across the country. Valencia has designated official observation points selected for clear sightlines and capacity. Hotels and wineries are offering eclipse-themed packages, and the City of Arts and Sciences has organized months of preparatory events.

Getting There

For those who can't make it to Spain, Iberia's livestream offers a front-row view from the best seat in the house — above the atmosphere. And for eclipse chasers already planning their trips, the Perseid meteor shower peaks on the same night, offering a celestial double feature for anyone with a clear western horizon after sunset.
